# typed-sql 2.2.0

typed-sql 2.2 updates the dependency graph, adds explicit recoverable project setup, and connects
the experimental editor backend to TypeScript 7.1 beta. Unsupported SQL continues to fail closed.

## Highlights

- Project setup can apply a reviewed plan, install dependencies with lifecycle scripts disabled,
  verify the installed language server, and recover an interrupted file application. Existing
  dependency ranges, custom scripts, and editor JSONC comments are preserved.
- Microsoft's native TypeScript client can launch typed-sql through packaged SDK executables on
  macOS, Linux, and Windows, keeping one TypeScript language provider. Schema changes, unsaved
  queries, restart recovery, workspace folders, and Windows file URI identity are covered.
- The TypeScript bridge uses the public beta `async`, `ast`, and `fs` APIs, with the beta dependency
  isolated from stable packages. Query compiler verification continues to use TypeScript 7.0.2.
- Dependency security fixes cover application adapters, tooling, editor clients, and publishing
  dependencies. Driver adapters remain explicit application dependencies.
- Publication retries reconcile missing npm tags without republishing immutable versions or
  moving newer versions backwards. Experimental companions remain explicitly experimental even
  when selected by versionless installation.

## Compatibility

The stable runtime and compiler require Node.js 22.11 or newer. The optional `node:sqlite` adapter
requires Node.js 22.13 or newer. PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite are stable dialect packages.

VS Code 1.140.0 is exercised by real host tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Zed 1.25.3 has manual
PostgreSQL baseline verification on macOS arm64, including a smoke check of the release WASM;
broader Zed dialect and editor-feature conformance is not claimed.

See the [compatibility matrix](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/reference/compatibility),
[editor setup](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/guides/editors), and
[upgrade guide](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/guides/upgrading-from-v1).

## Package tracks

The eleven-package stable train contains `@typed-sql/core`, `@typed-sql/opentelemetry`,
`@typed-sql/ast`, `@typed-sql/schema`, `@typed-sql/config`, `@typed-sql/compiler`,
`@typed-sql/conformance`, `@typed-sql/postgres`, `@typed-sql/mysql`, `@typed-sql/sqlite`, and
`@typed-sql/cli`.

`@typed-sql/ts-bridge`, `@typed-sql/language-server`, and the editor integrations remain
experimental. Their prerelease versions and package metadata retain that classification; stable
packages do not depend on them. An npm installation tag does not promote the preview contract.

## Evidence

The protected release workflow checks the exact release commit, packed database consumers,
registry-only candidate installation, vulnerability audit, and artifact integrity before stable
publication. Stable verification from npm precedes these aggregate release notes.
